We concentrate on the case of nearly\u2010\n                    <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink=\"http:\/\/www.w3.org\/1999\/xlink\" xlink:href=\"graphic\/prop201700034-math-0001.png\" xlink:title=\"urn:x-wiley:00158208:media:prop201700034:prop201700034-math-0001\"\/>\n                    gravity and discuss a very simple mechanical picture for the gravitational dynamics. We derive a formula for the two sided correlators that includes the effect of gravitational backreaction, which limits the amount of information we can send through the wormhole. We emphasize that the process can be viewed as a teleportation protocol where the teleportee feels nothing special as he\/she goes through the wormhole. We discuss some applications to the cloning paradox for old black holes. We point out that the same formula we derived for\n                    <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink=\"http:\/\/www.w3.org\/1999\/xlink\" xlink:href=\"graphic\/prop201700034-math-0002.png\" xlink:title=\"urn:x-wiley:00158208:media:prop201700034:prop201700034-math-0002\"\/>\n                    gravity is also valid for the simple SYK quantum mechanical theory, around the thermofield double state. We present a heuristic picture for this phenomenon in terms of an operator growth model.
